text:
ajit: Hey all, Ajit (new runtime eng). Trying to build from source on my M1 Mac — obviously no CUDA here. Whats the recommended dev path for someone without local NVIDIA hardware? :wave:
linh: welcome! we usually do CPU-only locally and hop onto a Linux GPU build host for anything nvcc-related.
omar: ^^^ don't fight mac + cuda. use the remote fleet or the gpu devcontainer.
ajit: cool. I tried `ssh build@buildfarm` but got permission denied. Is there a standard onboarding flow for SSH creds?
paige: @devops-bot new hires get short-lived certs via the access ticket. Please open a ticket in #help with your SSO and team.
devops-bot: please file a ticket. See /handbook/dev-onboarding -> "GPU build hosts" for the exact steps. Access is provisioned after manager approval.
ajit: thanks. while i wait, how do I avoid the configure step error where cmake insists on finding nvcc?
linh: run cmake with CUDA disabled: `cmake -DENABLE_CUDA=OFF -S . -B build/local` or set `export SKIP_CUDA_PROBE=1`. The top-level CMakeLists has a guard for that env var.
ajit: `SKIP_CUDA_PROBE=1` fixed configure but later the integration target fails linking to cudadevrt on the host: `ld: cannot find -lcudadevrt`. Any tips?
paige: on build hosts we load modules. Run `module load cuda/12.1` so CUDA libs are on LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Also ensure `CUDA_HOME` is set in the build environment.
ajit: loaded the module but hitting `ptxas: error: Unsupported gpu architecture 'compute_70'` — host is A100 (sm_80) but cmake is emitting compute_70.
omar: there's an env override. Set `export TARGET_ARCH=sm_80` before building, or edit `tools/select-kernels.sh` in your workspace.
ajit: setting TARGET_ARCH fixed ptxas. Thanks. Is there a docker image folks use for faster iterations?
sam: yes, we have `redwood/dev-gpu:latest` on the fleet. After you get SSH, you can `docker run --rm -it -v $PWD:/work redwood/dev-gpu:latest` and the entrypoint maps to our build scripts. For pure CPU work we also have `redwood/dev-cpu:stable`.
ajit: sweet. Last question: is there a short onboarding checklist for the runtime team first week?
linh: yep — clone + init submodules, `./scripts/bootstrap --dev`, build CPU with `SKIP_CUDA_PROBE=1`, run unit tests, file access ticket for GPU hosts, run `./scripts/build --target=gpu` on host, run `tools/perf/run_smoke.sh` once. Also reach out to your mentor for a pairing session on the first GPU smoke run.
ajit: awesome, i'll open the ticket and post the number here. thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
